title: MoUs and Information Sharing
summary: How information-sharing gateways and memoranda of understanding work, what a good MoU contains, and how to make and respond to cooperation requests effectively.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How information-sharing gateways and memoranda of understanding work, what a good MoU contains, and how to make and respond to cooperation requests effectively.
Learning Objectives: Explain information-sharing gateways and confidentiality constraints
Assess whether an MoU is fit for purpose
Prepare and respond to cross-border information requests
Syllabus: Bilateral and multilateral MoUs, including the IOSCO MMoU
Confidentiality, data protection and onward-sharing limits
Making a clear, proportionate cooperation request
Exercise: reviewing a sample MoU for strengths and gaps
Intended Audience: Supervisors responsible for cross-border groups, branches, subsidiaries or third-country firms
International affairs, legal and cooperation staff managing MoUs and information requests
Senior supervisors and managers who represent the authority in colleges and crisis management groups
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of prudential or conduct supervision is helpful. No prior involvement in colleges or international cooperation is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Supervisory Colleges (2014)
IOSCO, Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU) and Enhanced MMoU (2016)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
IAIS, Insurance Core Principles and Common Framework for the Supervision of Internationally Active Insurance Groups (ComFrame)
